verses.verse:
आरोहस्यावरोहस्य द्वे विधी वर्णिते धिया।
अहि मन्डूक वच्चैव गतिस्तत्र पृथक् पृथक्।१००।
verses.text: Two methods of ascent and descent are described with thought; the movement in them is, separately, like that of the snake and of the frog.

commentary.text: Wherever there is a question of climbing or descending, two kinds of method are possible: one sliding like a snake, and the other jumping like a frog. On this basis people build steps in their houses for climbing with the feet, and also build a separate slope for taking a bicycle up. If on the flute a long, channel-like hole were made from one hole to another, and one went from the first to the second note by sliding with some smooth metal, this would be called śrutisparśa (touching the śrutis) ascent or descent, because the sounds lying between the first hole, Sa, and the second hole, Re — which we call śrutis — are touched. To master this difficult action, flute players practise not only lifting the fingers but also lacāva (flexing) them. When you raise and set the finger on the hole many times while flexing it, the action of mīṇḍ (glide) will begin to happen. Flex it in whatever direction suits you, so that the hole opens slowly and closes slowly. If one note is far from the other, as in 'Sa Ma', flex the fingers together at the same time, so that the flexing is not broken anywhere.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
